Getting started

Source: vignettes/articles/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd
library(sasonr)

Run a SAS program

sas_run() takes SAS source code, runs it on the R engine and returns the log, the listing and the WORK data sets.

code <- "
data dm;
  input usubjid $ age sex $;
  datalines;
S01 45 M
S02 70 F
S03 .  F
;
run;

data adsl;
  set dm;
  length agegr1 $5;
  if missing(age) then agegr1 = 'Miss';
  else if age < 65 then agegr1 = '<65';
  else agegr1 = '>=65';
  put usubjid= age= agegr1=;
run;
"
res <- sas_run(code)
sas_log(res)
#> 1          
#> 2          data dm;
#> 3            input usubjid $ age sex $;
#> 4            datalines;
#> 
#> NOTE: The data set WORK.DM has 3 observations and 3 variables.
#> 8          ;
#> 9          run;
#> 10         
#> 11         data adsl;
#> 12           set dm;
#> 13           length agegr1 $5;
#> 14           if missing(age) then agegr1 = 'Miss';
#> 15           else if age < 65 then agegr1 = '<65';
#> 16           else agegr1 = '>=65';
#> 17           put usubjid= age= agegr1=;
#> 18         run;
#> 
#> usubjid=S01 age=45 agegr1=<65
#> usubjid=S02 age=70 agegr1=>=65
#> usubjid=S03 age=. agegr1=Miss
#> NOTE: There were 3 observations read from the data set WORK.DM.
#> NOTE: The data set WORK.ADSL has 3 observations and 4 variables.
res$work$adsl
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   usubjid   age sex   agegr1
#>   <chr>   <dbl> <chr> <chr> 
#> 1 S01        45 M     <65   
#> 2 S02        70 F     >=65  
#> 3 S03        NA F     Miss

Missing values have SAS semantics (a missing numeric value is smaller than any number), and character variables have a fixed length, here set by the LENGTH statement.

Translate a program into an R script

sas_script() writes the translation of a program as an R script that runs after library(sasonr). With tidy = TRUE, each vectorised DATA step becomes a dplyr pipe on R data frames (the script loads dplyr and tidylog, so every step reports what it did); steps that need sasonr’s own runtime run in a short session block.

code2 <- "
data lab;
  input usubjid $ visit aval;
  datalines;
S01 1 10
S01 2 12
S02 1 20
S02 2 18
;
run;

data chg;
  set lab;
  by usubjid;
  retain base;
  if first.usubjid then base = aval;
  chg = aval - base;
run;
"
sas_script(sas_translate(code2), tidy = TRUE)
#> # Translation of the SAS program, written by sasonr.
#> # Tidy form: steps that need a sasonr session run in a session block.
#> library(sasonr)
#> library(dplyr)
#> library(tidylog)
#> 
#> # data lab;  (SAS line 2)
#> lab <- sas_read_input(
#>   sas_infile_open(
#>     c("S01 1 10", "S01 2 12", "S02 1 20", "S02 2 18"),
#>     c(5L, 6L, 7L, 8L),
#>     opts = list(lines = 1L, end_text = ";")
#>   ),
#>   list(
#>     items = list(
#>       list(
#>         k = "var",
#>         name = "usubjid",
#>         disp = "usubjid",
#>         char = TRUE,
#>         len = 8L,
#>         mode = "list"
#>       ),
#>       list(
#>         k = "var",
#>         name = "visit",
#>         disp = "visit",
#>         char = FALSE,
#>         len = NA_integer_,
#>         mode = "list"
#>       ),
#>       list(
#>         k = "var",
#>         name = "aval",
#>         disp = "aval",
#>         char = FALSE,
#>         len = NA_integer_,
#>         mode = "list"
#>       )
#>     ),
#>     hold = ""
#>   )
#> ) |>
#>   select(usubjid, visit, aval)
#> 
#> # data chg;  (SAS line 12)
#> chg <- lab |>
#>   sas_check_sorted("usubjid", FALSE) |>
#>   mutate(first.usubjid = sas_first(usubjid)) |>
#>   group_by(.grp = cumsum(first.usubjid)) |>
#>   mutate(base = as.numeric(dplyr::first(aval))) |>
#>   ungroup() |>
#>   mutate(chg = sas_arith(aval, base, "-")) |>
#>   select(usubjid, visit, aval, base, chg)

Without tidy, every SAS step becomes one call of a step verb on a session: sas_data_step() holds the generated code of a DATA step and the SAS text it came from, sas_proc_sort() and sas_proc_means() show the options the program gave, and other steps keep their SAS text. This script gives the same WORK data sets and the same log as sas_run().

code3 <- "
data adsl;
  input usubjid $ age;
  datalines;
S01 70
S02 41
;
run;
proc sort data=adsl out=bysubj; by descending age; run;
"
sas_script(sas_translate(code3))
#> # Translation of the SAS program, written by sasonr.
#> library(sasonr)
#> 
#> s <- sas_session()
#> 
#> s |> sas_data_step("adsl", \(work) {
#>   # ---- DATA ADSL (SAS line 2) -- level L1
#>   # L1: no cross-row state
#>   .d <- sas_read_input(
#>     sas_infile_open(
#>       c("S01 70", "S02 41"),
#>       c(5L, 6L),
#>       opts = list(lines = 1L, end_text = ";")
#>     ),
#>     list(
#>       items = list(
#>         list(
#>           k = "var",
#>           name = "usubjid",
#>           disp = "usubjid",
#>           char = TRUE,
#>           len = 8L,
#>           mode = "list"
#>         ),
#>         list(
#>           k = "var",
#>           name = "age",
#>           disp = "age",
#>           char = FALSE,
#>           len = NA_integer_,
#>           mode = "list"
#>         )
#>       ),
#>       hold = ""
#>     )
#>   )
#>   work$adsl <- .d |> dplyr::select(usubjid, age)
#> }, sas = r"(data adsl;
#>   input usubjid $ age;
#>   datalines;
#> S01 70
#> S02 41
#> ;)", line = 2L)
#> 
#> s |> sas_proc_sort("data=adsl out=bysubj", by = "descending age", line = c(9L, 9L))

sas_script() also takes the result of sas_run(): the script is then the trace of that run, including the steps that macro code generated.

Look at the code of one step

sas_translate() returns the generated R code step by step, for debugging. Simple steps become vectorised dplyr pipelines; steps with cross-row state such as RETAIN, LAG or FIRST./LAST. use grouped vectorised code when the result can be proven identical, and an explicit row loop otherwise. The header of each step names its level and the reason.

tr <- sas_translate(code2)
cat(tr$steps[[2]]$code)
#> # ---- DATA CHG (SAS line 12) -- level L2
#> # L2: BY-group processing (FIRST./LAST.); retained value carried forward (baseline / LOCF)
#> .d <- sas_ds(work, "lab") |>
#>   sas_note_read("lab") |>
#>   sas_check_sorted("usubjid", FALSE) |>
#>   dplyr::mutate(first.usubjid = sas_first(usubjid)) |>
#>   dplyr::group_by(.grp = cumsum(first.usubjid)) |>
#>   dplyr::mutate(base = as.numeric(dplyr::first(aval))) |>
#>   dplyr::ungroup() |>
#>   dplyr::mutate(chg = sas_arith(aval, base, "-", .at = c(17L, 14L)))
#> work$chg <- .d |> dplyr::select(usubjid, visit, aval, base, chg)
sas_run(code2)$work$chg
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   usubjid visit  aval  base   chg
#>   <chr>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 S01         1    10    10     0
#> 2 S01         2    12    10     2
#> 3 S02         1    20    20     0
#> 4 S02         2    18    20    -2

Macro language

Macro processing and step execution interleave: a step is run as soon as it is complete, so values created with CALL SYMPUTX are available to the macro code that follows.

code3 <- "
%macro check(ds);
  data _null_;
    call symputx('n', 3);
  run;
  %if &n > 2 %then %put NOTE: &ds is large;
  %else %put NOTE: &ds is small;
%mend check;
%check(adsl)
"
sas_log(sas_run(code3), echo = FALSE)
#> NOTE: adsl is large

echo = FALSE leaves the program lines out: the log shows only the messages and the PUT output.

Unsupported features fail loudly

sasonr never guesses. A feature it does not support stops the program with a classed condition that carries the SAS line number.

sas_run("data a; x = 1; run; proc report data=a; run;")
#> Error in `sasonr_abort()`:
#> ! Unsupported: PROC REPORT (SAS line 1)

The same applies by default (sasonr.strict = TRUE) to functions, formats and informats whose status in the feature registry is approximate (the last bits of numeric results may not be exact, for example in the probability functions) or unsupported: they stop with a sasonr_strict_error condition (see ?sasonr_strict).

sas_run("data a; p = probnorm(1.96); run;")
#> Error in `strict_gate()`:
#> ! function PROBNORM is approximate; set options(sasonr.strict = FALSE) to use it (SAS line 1)

To run them anyway, with a warning of class sasonr_strict_warning, turn strict mode off:

old <- options(sasonr.strict = FALSE)
res <- suppressWarnings(sas_run("data a; p = probnorm(1.96); run;"))
res$work$a$p
#> [1] 0.9750021
options(old)
